label: the shift count is not masked to five bits
why: ia32's SAR masks its count operand to five bits, and GCC lowers a non-constant `>>` to exactly that instruction -- measured, not argued: compiling both forms and diffing the text shows the masked one costs one extra `and $0x1e,%ecx` and changes nothing else.  What is held fixed is the target and the lowering, over the WHOLE range of vect_idx and not a sample; the object itself has no `and`, so the mask is this reconstruction's, written so that an out-of-range index is defined C rather than undefined.  The sweep in t_v34k56.c drives vect_idx to 8, 15, 100, -1 and -9 and the blob agrees with the masked form at every one, which is what makes the mask right rather than merely safe.

label: the Ja arm does not consult the bit source at all
why: The directly called, nonvirtual getK56FlexJaBits in this same blob is exactly three bytes, `xor %eax,%eax; ret`: it returns zero and writes nothing through the supplied pointer for every object and input.  Replacing that call with `done = 0` therefore preserves every observable result of the fixed linked blob.  The call remains in the reconstruction because its relocation and bytes matter to object identity; this classification is behavioral, not permission to remove it.
